targets.why: The plan puts the About surface behind a new control in this window (an in-app <dialog> opened from the main view), so this is the surface the feature changes. The baseline is what makes the addition legible: today there is no About control anywhere in the app, and no attribution.

The surface the feature exists for: the modal itself, showing the 'Created by Clint Parker' attribution and the clintparker.com link. Added in the `after` pass because it does not exist in the baseline — there is deliberately no `before/about-dialog-*.png`.

notes: mode: before, captured pre-implementation. The branch holds only spec/plan/tasks commits (cce5ec2), no implementation, so this is a true baseline rather than a reconstruction.

FEATURE IDENTITY — the primary checkout's .specify/run-context.json names 20260813-105424-urls-clickable-and, which is the PREVIOUS, already-merged feature (it is in `git branch --merged main`). It was not used. This run is 20260813-175859-clint-parker-about, agreed on by three independent sources: the primary's .specify/run.lock (run_id 20260814T005916Z-20260813-175859-clint-parker-about), this worktree's own .specify/run-context.json (same run_id), and check-prerequisites.sh --paths-only --json run with SPECIFY_INIT_DIR/SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY set, which resolved this same FEATURE_DIR.

CAPTURE METHOD DEVIATION — the profile's capture_method (AppleScript window resize + `screencapture -R` against process `tauri-app`) was impossible this run: the Mac's screen is LOCKED (CGSSessionScreenIsLocked true), so `screencapture -R` fails with 'could not create image from rect' and a full-screen capture would only yield the lock screen. Accessibility/System Events was available, but with no capturable window it is of no use.

FALLBACK USED — the shipped frontend was driven through Vite (`pnpm dev`, port 1420) in Chromium via Playwright, with window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__ stubbed in an init script (transformCallback/unregisterCallback/invoke, plus plugin:event|listen). The real src/main.ts, src/render.ts, src/form.ts, src/open.ts, index.html and src/styles.css render these images — only the Rust IPC layer is replaced. What is NOT represented: the native window chrome/title bar, WKWebView-vs-Chromium font rasterisation, and real check timing.

The `after` pass must use this same method for a comparable pair unless the screen is unlocked by then; if it captures the real Tauri window instead, say so rather than presenting the pair as like-for-like.

Clock frozen to 1786665600000 (2026-08-14T00:00:00Z) via a Date.now override, and each status stamped 12s earlier, so the 'Last checked' column reads '12s ago' in both modes instead of drifting with the 1s repaint timer.

Statuses were delivered as synthetic `site-status` events (one Up, one Down with reason 'DNS lookup failed') rather than by waiting on real network checks — no request leaves the machine, and the Pending state resolves deterministically. The feature does not touch the Pending state, so capturing the resolved states is the more useful baseline.

The user's real ~/Library/Application Support/com.clintparker.site-checker/sites.json was NEVER touched — the browser route seeds sites in memory over the stubbed IPC, so the profile's backup/restore dance was unnecessary. Verified unchanged after the run (mtime 2026-08-10 15:22, md5 27364d6a5bad0746748bf046ffc15ba8). autostart.initialized was likewise left alone.

specs/*/screenshots/ is ignored by the repo-root .gitignore:44. Resolved once, in a committed file, by adding `!screenshots/` to this feature directory's own .gitignore — `git check-ignore` now reports the directory and the PNGs as not ignored, so a plain `git add` tracks them and the PR's links will resolve. No `git add -f` was used.

Judgement calls made unattended: one target (main-window) rather than several, because the feature adds a single surface reachable from it; the empty state and the add/edit form are untouched by this feature and were not captured.
--- mode: after (captured against 89d0cf9, implementation commit 4333962 'feat(about)') ---

AFTER — feature identity re-resolved from scratch and reached the same answer. The primary checkout's .specify/run-context.json STILL names the previous, already-merged 20260813-105424-urls-clickable-and, so the documented lookup order answers WRONG here rather than empty. It was not used. This worktree's own .specify/run-context.json carries run_id 20260814T005916Z-20260813-175859-clint-parker-about, identical to the primary's .specify/run.lock, and check-prerequisites.sh --paths-only --json (run from this worktree with SPECIFY_INIT_DIR/SPECIFY_FEATURE_DIRECTORY exported) resolved FEATURE_DIR to this same directory. Three sources agree; the before and after images are the same feature.

AFTER — the screen was STILL locked (ioreg IOConsoleLocked true), so the profile's native `screencapture` path remained impossible and the before pass's Vite+Playwright harness was reproduced deliberately, exactly as the note above required. The pair is like-for-like: same URL, same stub surface, same frozen clock (1786665600000), same two seed sites, same two synthetic `site-status` events stamped 12s earlier. The same caveats therefore apply to BOTH sets — no native window chrome, Chromium rather than WKWebView rasterisation, no real network timing. Neither set shows the real Tauri window.

AFTER — the harness gained exactly one stub the baseline did not need: `plugin:app|version`, returning "0.0.0". The implementation's About dialog reads its version through `getVersion()` from @tauri-apps/api/app, which routes to that command rather than to a project `invoke`. "0.0.0" is the app's genuine local-build sentinel (package.json version, replaced from the pushed tag by release.yml), so the version line in these images reads as it does on any local build — it is not an invented value.

AFTER — both viewports were captured at deviceScaleFactor 1, matching the baseline's actual pixel dimensions (720x480 and 480x320). A first attempt at 2x was discarded and re-shot rather than committed: a 1440x960 'after' beside a 720x480 'before' is not a comparable pair.

AFTER — the `about-dialog` target has NO baseline counterpart, by construction: the dialog did not exist before this feature. `before/` holds main-window only; `after/` holds both targets. The main-window pair is the comparable one, and it differs in exactly one visible way — the new 'About' button in the footer's right side, opposite 'Launch at login'.

AFTER — verified from the rendered DOM, not just by eye: the dialog's text reads 'Site Checker' / 'Version 0.0.0' / 'Created by Clint Parker' / 'clintparker.com' / 'Close', and all four captures completed with zero page errors and zero console errors. The narrow (480x320) capture confirms the modal still fits and stays legible at the window's resizable floor.

AFTER — the link was NOT clicked during capture. `open_url` is stubbed to a no-op recorder, so activating it would prove nothing about the real backend opener and would only risk closing the dialog mid-shot. QA (qa/qa-20260814-015212.md) is what exercises that path.

AFTER — the user's real sites.json was again never touched; re-verified after the run at mtime 2026-08-10 15:22, md5 27364d6a5bad0746748bf046ffc15ba8, byte-identical to the baseline reading. autostart.initialized left alone. The Vite dev server ran from the worktree, logged to /tmp (outside the checkout), and was killed afterwards with port 1420 confirmed free.

AFTER — no application code was modified by this step. The capture harness lives at /tmp/site-checker-shots-after-20260814/capture.mjs, outside the checkout, and nothing outside FEATURE_DIR/screenshots/ was committed.
